name: neronvain

special_abilities.name: draconic majesty
special_abilities.desc: Neronvain adds his Charisma bonus to his AC (included).

special_abilities.name: fey ancestry
special_abilities.desc: Magic can't put Neronvain to sleep.

actions.name: multiattack
actions.desc: Neronvain makes two attacks, either with his shortsword or Eldritch Arrow.

actions.name: shortsword
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) poison damage.

actions.name: eldritch arrow
actions.desc: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d10) force damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.

actions.name: poisonous cloud (2/day)
actions.desc: Poison gas fills a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point Neronvain can see within 50 feet of him. The gas spreads around corners and remains until the start of Neronvain's next turn. Each creature that starts its turn in the gas must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

lore:
The figure known as Neronvain is less a man and more a lingering rot within the heart of the Misty Forest. Once a scion of elven royalty, he has become a phantom of the viridian gloom, inextricably bound to the ancient green wyrm, Chuth. Their habitat is a suffocating tapestry of ancient oaks and eternal fog, where the air itself tastes of pine needles and stagnant bile.

Neronvain’s predation is a masterclass in psychological cruelty. He does not merely hunt; he orchestrates. Using the dragon’s toxic breath as a shroud, he strikes from the emerald canopy with a grace that mocks his noble lineage. He targets the hope of his victims, isolating them through whispers and manufactured shadows before the final, venomous blow.

Local woodcutters speak of him in hushed tones as the "Gilded Traitor." To the elves, he is a cautionary tale of pride curdled into malice—a prince who traded his crown for a dragon’s leash. Folklore claims that when the mist thickens to the color of bruised moss, Neronvain is near, seeking to reclaim his lost kingdom through blood and blight.
